purpose: Hourly integration/value review delta: legacy manufacturing ERP plus learning/competency and EHS coverage. All evidence remains spec-level; no vendor sandbox or tenant credentials were used and writes remain disabled.

patch.evidenceNote: SAP Business One Service Layer exposes OData/REST business entities and actions. SAP states OData v3 is deprecated and OData v4 is the primary Service Layer protocol from FP 2405; new WFM adapters should use v4.

requiredPermissions: read-only Service Layer identity limited to required company/entities
dataAvailableOrExpected: production-order and ERP entities exposed by Service Layer
business partners/orders/inventory/finance context exposed by authorised entities
OData metadata and queryable entity sets
automationOpportunities: approved write-back only after sandbox write/read-back proof
customerValue: reuse SAP Business One operational data for staffing demand
savingsHypotheses: reduce over/under staffing against production demand
dataGaps: enabled entities, user-defined fields and company databases are customer specific
constraintsRisks: OData v3 is deprecated; v4 is the required new-build path
Service Layer is write-capable, so WFM discovery must remain read-only

patch.evidenceNote: Business Central online exposes standard/custom REST API v2.0 endpoints authenticated with Microsoft Entra ID. On-premises API services are disabled by default and use installation-specific authentication. Microsoft recommends APIs over older OData web-service patterns for new integrations.

requiredPermissions: Entra/application permissions or customer-scoped user permissions for required companies
on-prem API enablement where applicable
dataAvailableOrExpected: custom API entities where manufacturing-specific data is not present in the standard API
automationOpportunities: customer custom API ingestion for manufacturing-specific objects
customerValue: reuse Business Central data without bespoke database access
lower implementation effort through standard APIs
savingsHypotheses: improve staffing decisions when customer manufacturing/order signals are exposed
dataGaps: manufacturing-specific objects may require customer/partner custom API pages
online and on-prem authentication/enablement differ
constraintsRisks: on-prem APIs can be disabled and version lag is partner-controlled
custom API schema/version must be fingerprinted per tenant

patch.evidenceNote: Intuit documents the QuickBooks Online Accounting API as REST-based with OAuth 2.0, webhooks and sandbox companies. WFM should use it for finance/cost attribution rather than infer manufacturing execution data from QBO.

Deputy documents a JSON REST API, OAuth 2.0, webhooks for resources/actions, employee and timesheet integrations and sales-data ingestion. Advanced employee information requires additional vendor security review.

requiredPermissions: OAuth scopes/token access limited to employees, schedules/timesheets and required business metrics
dataAvailableOrExpected: sales/workload metrics where customer uses them
customerValue: reuse existing workforce data during migration/coexistence
savingsHypotheses: reduce payroll corrections and manual imports
reduce implementation effort where Deputy is already present
dataGaps: confidential employee data requires additional vendor approval
not all customer scheduling rules map one-to-one
constraintsRisks: webhook delivery must be idempotent/deduplicated
per-install custom scripts are not a portable integration strategy

requiredPermissions: OAuth bearer access to required SuccessFactors/Learning OData services
learning-history/competency scopes only where needed
automationOpportunities: remove scheduling eligibility when required training expires or changes revision
restore eligibility when verified completion arrives
assign/recommend retraining after engineering or safety change; write only after separate proof
savingsHypotheses: avoid production disruption from missing qualifications
dataGaps: customer learning item taxonomy must map to WFM skills/roles
learning write-back has documented limits and permissions

training history is qualification evidence only when customer policy maps it to a role/skill requirement

team hierarchy limited to required employees
View/GET-only API Suite permission during discovery

configured public API resources documented by tenant Swagger/OpenAPI

team hierarchy/security determines visible employees

systems.name: Oracle JD Edwards EnterpriseOne
systems.evidenceNote: Oracle EnterpriseOne AIS Server publishes REST APIs and Swagger/OpenAPI catalog endpoints for orchestrations. Exact manufacturing objects depend on the customer's EnterpriseOne applications and orchestrations.

requiredPermissions: AIS identity limited to approved orchestrations/data requests
read-only orchestrations for initial proof
dataAvailableOrExpected: orchestration metadata via Open API catalog
customer-defined manufacturing/finance data exposed by authorised orchestrations
automationOpportunities: reuse customer orchestrations to feed WFM demand/cost context
publish approved WFM outcomes only after controlled write certification
customerValue: support legacy manufacturing ERP estates without database scraping
savingsHypotheses: extend WFM to plants not yet migrated off JDE
dataGaps: available orchestrations and business functions are customer specific
legacy/custom JDE versions require compatibility discovery
constraintsRisks: orchestrations may be write-capable
API/catalog version and AIS configuration vary by estate

systems.name: Oracle E-Business Suite
systems.evidenceNote: Oracle E-Business Suite Integrated SOA Gateway exposes seeded/custom Integration Repository interfaces as REST and SOAP services; Oracle Integration also supports EBS business events and XML Gateway messages. Exact enabled interfaces are customer-specific.

requiredPermissions: grants only to required Integration Repository services/interfaces
read-only interface/view access for initial proof
dataAvailableOrExpected: open interface views and business events where enabled
automationOpportunities: reuse Oracle Integration where customer already has it
approved result write-back only after service-specific proof
savingsHypotheses: extend WFM without forcing ERP replacement
dataGaps: service exposure is administrator-configured and interface-specific
older EBS estates may use different authentication/service patterns
constraintsRisks: REST/SOAP services can be write-capable
WADL/WSDL and grants must be discovered per tenant/version

systems.name: Cornerstone OnDemand
systems.evidenceNote: Cornerstone exposes REST APIs secured with OAuth 2.0 client credentials and granular scopes. Learning APIs include transcript/task reads and learning assignments; bulk/reporting APIs exist for larger data volumes.

requiredPermissions: OAuth client credentials with transcript:read/task:read and only required learning scopes
service-account security permissions constrained to relevant populations
dataAvailableOrExpected: employee references and reporting/bulk exports where licensed
automationOpportunities: assign training when WFM identifies a skill/compliance gap
remove/reinstate scheduling eligibility from transcript state
savingsHypotheses: reduce production/compliance disruption caused by expired training
dataGaps: single-user transcript endpoints require bulk/reporting APIs for scale
custom transcript fields are not returned by some APIs
constraintsRisks: learning-assignment writes are real operations and remain disabled until sandbox proof
service-account permissions can further restrict OAuth scope

systems.name: Docebo
systems.evidenceNote: Docebo exposes REST APIs across Learn, Skills, Manage, Certification and related services. OAuth 2.0 is the standard third-party authentication path. The interactive API Browser acts on real tenant data, so WFM testing must not use mutative browser operations without authorisation.

requiredPermissions: OAuth application scoped to required read endpoints
Power User/resource visibility limited to required branches/populations
automationOpportunities: training assignment triggered by skill gap after separate write proof
savingsHypotheses: reduce time to productive deployment for new starters
avoid shifts staffed by workers missing required learning
dataGaps: additional/custom fields are tenant-defined and not fully described in generic API docs
visibility depends on assigned resources/catalogs
constraintsRisks: API Browser can execute real mutations
secondary identifiers may be mutable/non-unique; internal IDs should be canonical where possible

systems.name: Moodle
systems.evidenceNote: Moodle provides an External Services/Web Services framework with site-specific API documentation, token authentication and REST clients. Exposed functions are explicitly selected per service and capability.

requiredPermissions: dedicated external service exposing only required functions
authorised service user/token with least required capabilities
dataAvailableOrExpected: badges/custom fields where functions are enabled
site-specific plugin data through custom external functions
automationOpportunities: new-starter course assignment only after separate write proof
custom plugin/event bridge for site-specific skills
savingsHypotheses: avoid replacing an existing LMS purely for WFM integration
dataGaps: available functions vary by site/plugins

plugin/custom-service changes require version and schema checks

dedicated user/API key restricted to required applications and records
dataAvailableOrExpected: tenant application objects exposed through Intelex API v2
EHS/QMS records configured in the customer's application model
users/reference data required to reconcile safety/compliance records
automationOpportunities: remove/review scheduling eligibility after qualifying safety/compliance event
savingsHypotheses: reduce repeat incidents through shift/role pattern analysis
